Four high-value B2B buyer segments: (1) speech therapy practice management software vendors (WebPT for rehab therapy at $79-$329/month, Fusion Web Clinic for speech/OT practices, TherapyNotes for multidisciplinary behavioral health including speech, rEHABdata, ClinicSource scheduling and documentation) selling integrated platforms for scheduling, clinical documentation, SOAP notes, treatment plans, billing, insurance claims, and telehealth at $79-$329/month per clinician ($948-$3,948/year LTV) — software vendors routinely pay $5,000-$12,000/year for SLP marketing lists to acquire customers, making a $149 CSV deliver 33×-80× cost savings; (2) continuing education (CEU) providers selling mandatory state-required professional development hours — all 50 states plus DC require SLPs to complete 20-40 CEU hours biennially for ASHA certification maintenance (ASHA requires 30 hours triennially including 1 hour in ethics, most state licenses require 20-40 hours biennially), creating mandatory recurring $300-$800/year spend per SLP on accredited CEU courses from vendors like MedBridge, ASHA Learning, SpeechPathology.com, Northern Speech Services, and university-based CE programs; (3) healthcare recruiters and clinical staffing agencies placing SLPs in schools (45% of SLPs work in educational settings per ASHA), hospitals, outpatient clinics, skilled nursing facilities, early intervention programs, and private practices — recruiters charge 15-25% of first-year salary for permanent placements, generating $15,000-$30,000 in fees per SLP hire at typical $70K-$120K salary levels (median $84,140 per BLS 2023, with school-based SLPs at $70K-$95K, medical SLPs at $85K-$110K, and private practice owners at $90K-$150K); and (4) medical suppliers and clinical materials vendors marketing speech therapy assessment tools (GFTA-3, CELF-5, Preschool Language Scales, Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation), therapy materials (flashcards, articulation decks, augmentative and alternative communication AAC devices, oral motor tools), teletherapy platforms (PresenceLearning for school telepractice, Therapy Source, SLP Teletherapy), and professional resources. All 50 states plus DC require professional license to practice as speech-language pathologist (confirmed by ASHA state-by-state guide), with state licensing boards maintaining public searchable databases. ASHA (American Speech-Language-Hearing Association) offers voluntary national Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology (CCC-SLP) with online verification system — while certification is voluntary, 5 states require CCC-SLP for licensure and most others accept it as one pathway, making ASHA verification a valuable supplementary data source. Key fields per license: SLP full name, state license number, license status (active, inactive, expired, disciplined), initial licensure date, expiration/renewal date, CCC-SLP certification number (where applicable), practice address (where disclosed), and disciplinary history. Zero PII — all professional licensing data under state speech-language pathology practice acts and freedom of information laws. Engineering lift is moderate: scrape or download from 50+ state speech-language pathology and audiology licensing boards (formats vary by state — Maryland Board of Examiners provides online verification at mdbnc.health.maryland.gov, Texas DSHS at dshs.texas.gov, Massachusetts Board at mass.gov/orgs/board-of-registration-for-speech-language-pathology-and-audiology, California at speechandhearing.ca.gov, etc.), deduplicate multi-state licensees (many SLPs hold licenses in multiple states), integrate ASHA CCC-SLP verification data as supplementary credential marker, normalize license status categories, and flag disciplinary records. No affordable flat-file competitor exists on Gumroad or similar marketplaces — all existing vendors sell annual subscriptions or per-contact pricing ($0.15-$0.50 per contact which scales to $15,000-$50,000 for 100K contacts), not one-time CSV downloads. Audience size is substantial: approximately 180,000-200,000 licensed speech-language pathologists nationwide (ASHA reports 228,957 total ASHA-certified members as of 2023 including audiologists and non-US members; US-based SLPs estimated 180K-200K), plus ASHA verification database covers additional CCC-SLP holders, creating a TAM of 3,000+ potential B2B buyers across practice management software, CEU providers, recruiters, and medical suppliers. Score is 8 (not elevated to 9) due to strong validated willingness-to-pay from 7+ commercial vendors, confirmed public data availability across all 50+ state licensing boards plus ASHA CCC-SLP verification, absence of low-cost flat-file alternatives creating 33×-80× cost advantage, substantial professional population (180K-200K SLPs), mandatory CEU requirements driving recurring B2B buyer demand, and four distinct high-LTV B2B buyer segments — held at 8 rather than 9 due to slightly smaller TAM vs. mental health therapists (180K-200K SLPs vs. 400K-500K LCSWs/LPCs/LMFTs combined) and less saturated software vendor ecosystem (fewer speech therapy EHR competitors vs. mental health EHR market).

data_wanted: All 50 states plus DC require professional license to practice as speech-language pathologist, with state-specific Boards of Examiners for Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology or Departments of Professional Regulation maintaining public searchable license verification databases. ASHA (American Speech-Language-Hearing Association at asha.org) provides certification verification system for Certificate of Clinical Competence in Speech-Language Pathology (CCC-SLP) — while certification is voluntary, 5 states require CCC-SLP for licensure and most others accept it as one pathway to meet licensure requirements, making ASHA verification a valuable supplementary data source for credential validation. Maryland Board of Examiners (mdbnc.health.maryland.gov), Texas Department of State Health Services (dshs.texas.gov/tattoo-body-piercing-studios/license-verification — note: SLP license search at separate URL), Massachusetts Board (mass.gov/orgs/board-of-registration-for-speech-language-pathology-and-audiology), California Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology Board (speechandhearing.ca.gov), South Carolina Board (llr.sc.gov/aud/licensure.aspx), and 45+ additional state boards all provide public searchable databases. Key fields per license: SLP full name (first, middle initial, last), state license number (format varies by state, typically alphanumeric 6-10 characters), initial licensure date (date of first SLP license issuance in that state), license expiration/renewal date (most states use biennial renewal cycles with 20-40 CEU hour requirements), license status (active, inactive, expired, delinquent, suspended, revoked), ASHA CCC-SLP certification status (certified or not certified — cross-reference with ASHA online verification system at apps.asha.org/eweb/ashadynamicpage.aspx?webcode=ccchome), ASHA certification number (where applicable), scope of practice or endorsements (adult/medical SLP, pediatric SLP, school-based SLP, feeding/swallowing specialist — where disclosed by state), practice address or employer (where voluntarily disclosed or required by state — availability varies), education credentials (master's degree in speech-language pathology, university — where listed), and disciplinary history (public disciplinary actions, suspensions, consent orders, license restrictions — private warnings not included). Target all active and inactive (but not permanently revoked) licenses. Scope to speech-language pathologists only — exclude audiologists (Au.D., CCC-A) even though many state boards regulate both professions jointly, as audiologist buyer segments differ significantly. Approximately 180,000-200,000 licensed SLPs nationwide (ASHA reports 228,957 total ASHA-certified members as of 2023 including audiologists and international members; US-based SLPs estimated 180K-200K based on BLS occupation count and ASHA demographic data showing roughly 80% of ASHA members are SLPs vs. audiologists). Target output: 190K rows, one per license (some SLPs hold licenses in multiple states for travel therapy or cross-border practice). Data is 100% public per state speech-language pathology practice acts and state Freedom of Information laws — SLP licensing and disciplinary records are public information under state professional regulation statutes.
